_comment: FROZEN from the live book on 2026-08-18, the day positions() was found displaying levels the monitor had rejected. Each case states its expected result INDEPENDENTLY of the code, so a change that alters behaviour fails here instead of in production. Do not regenerate these from the code they test.

cases.name: XOM — agent stop looser, no widen, one target against two
cases.why: The 10:35 session opened XOM and set stop 155.00 / target 172.00. Both were refused: the stop for being below the thesis stop without widen, the target for being one where the thesis carries two. positions() displayed them as if in force.

cases.name: MRK — explicit widen WITH a reason applies a looser stop
cases.why: The one override actually in force on 2026-08-18, and the one the enforcement report got wrong because server.py never passed the widen flag.

override.reason: inherited stop sits inside the name's own noise

cases.read_model_why: positions() always resolves guard-on, because the live monitor always passes a prices dict. With no quote for this symbol the override is refused and the thesis stop is what is watched — even though the apply_overrides(prices=None) path above skips that guard.

cases.name: TER — stop refused, targets ACCEPTED (count matches)
cases.why: Proves refusal is per-field. TER supplied two targets against a two-target thesis, so those applied while its looser stop did not. The 15:15 session quoted 390.9603 and was right; the display said 385.00 and was wrong.

cases.name: widen claimed with a BLANK reason does not apply
cases.why: The monitor requires widen AND a reason. A blank reason must not loosen a stop.

cases.name: a tighter stop applies with no widen needed
cases.read_model_why: positions() always resolves guard-on, because the live monitor always passes a prices dict. With no quote for this symbol the override is refused and the thesis stop is what is watched — even though the apply_overrides(prices=None) path above skips that guard.

cases.name: a stop at or above the live price is refused (would arm already breached)
a corrupt live price refuses the override rather than sailing through
cases.why: A NaN quote once let a stale override be APPLIED over a thesis stop.

cases.name: no override at all is silent and keeps the thesis
an EMPTY target list is not an override and is not a refusal
cases.read_model_why: positions() always resolves guard-on, because the live monitor always passes a prices dict. With no quote for this symbol the override is refused and the thesis stop is what is watched — even though the apply_overrides(prices=None) path above skips that guard.

cases.name: targets move in EITHER direction when the count matches
cases.why: Raising a target adds no downside; blocking it is why nothing here has reached a take-profit.

cases.name: price looked up and MISSING — the guard fails closed (the live monitor's mode)
cases.why: The production monitor always passes a prices dict, so a symbol with no quote has its override DROPPED. positions() must fail closed identically or it shows a level the monitor is not using. This case was added after the replay caught exactly that divergence in the display on 2026-08-18.

cases.name: stale ownership — a thesis with no live position still resolves, and says which stop would apply
cases.why: Codex listed stale ownership among the cases to freeze. The monitor only watches symbols in its held set, so resolution for an unowned name must not crash and must not imply anything is being watched. Ownership is decided upstream (owned_symbols); the resolver's job is only to say which level WOULD be in force.

override.reason: tightened before the position was sold
